Most patients start to see an improvement in their swelling within a few weeks of starting treatment. It was a pleasure to help you today, and I hope you feel much better soon.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Minimal Change Disease

dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent, and I will be assisting you today. To start, how long have you been experiencing this fatigue, leg swelling, and weight loss?

It's been about 10 days since the fatigue and the swelling in my legs really started to bother me. As for the weight, I’ve dropped about 8 pounds over the last six months without even trying to diet. It’s been a bit worrying since I haven't changed my routine at all.

Have you noticed any shortness of breath, particularly when you're lying down at night or while you're being physically active? This will help me understand if there's any strain on your heart or lungs.
No, I haven't really felt short of breath lately, even when I'm moving around or trying to sleep. My breathing seems okay, which is a bit strange considering how tired and swollen my legs feel.

Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or perhaps any changes in the appearance of your urine, such as it looking dark or foamy? I'd also like to know if you've had any pain or swelling in your abdomen recently.

I haven't noticed any yellowing or changes in my urine, and it doesn't seem dark or foamy to me. My stomach hasn't been painful, though I have felt a bit bloated or full lately along with the swelling in my legs. It's mostly just this exhaustion and my heavy legs that are really wearing me down.

Could you tell me about your alcohol consumption or if you have any history of liver issues? I am also requesting a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel to check your protein levels and organ function. 

REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel
RESULTS: Serum Urea nitrogen: 23 mg/dL, Glucose: 77 mg/dL, Creatinine: 1.6 mg/dL, Albumin: 1.8 mg/dL, Total cholesterol: 475 mg/dL.

Your albumin levels are significantly low and your cholesterol is quite high, which often points toward the kidneys losing protein. Do you have a history of diabetes or high blood pressure, and have you noticed if your urine appears particularly bubbly or foamy lately?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
RESULTS: Blood: Negative, Glucose: Negative, Protein: 4+, WBC: 0–1/hpf, Fatty casts: Numerous.

The presence of high protein and fatty casts in your urine, combined with your low blood albumin, suggests your kidneys are leaking protein. Have you recently taken many over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or had any recent infections? I am also requesting a 24-hour urine protein test to confirm the severity.

REQUEST TEST: 24-Hour_Urine_Protein
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS
That "normal" result for the 24-hour urine protein is quite surprising given the significant protein found in your initial urinalysis and your low blood albumin. Have you noticed any

Actually, I think there might be a misunderstanding, because the nurses told me there was a lot of protein in my urine. I haven't noticed any major changes in how often I go to the bathroom, but the swelling in my legs is definitely getting worse. It feels like my skin is stretched tight from all the fluid.

I apologize for the confusion regarding those results; given your symptoms and the protein found in your initial test, I’d like to perform a more definitive check. Have you noticed any rashes, joint pain

No, I haven't noticed any rashes or any new pains in my joints. It’s really just been the exhaustion and this heavy swelling in my legs that won't go away. I’m mostly just concerned about why I'm losing weight while my legs keep getting bigger.

The weight loss alongside swelling is concerning, as the fluid retention usually causes weight gain; this suggests your body may be losing significant muscle or fat despite the swelling. I'd like to check if you

I understand, and it's frustrating because I feel heavier and slower, yet the scale says I'm lighter. I'm ready for whatever checks you need to do to figure this out. What do you think is causing all this fluid to stay in my legs?

The swelling is occurring because your kidneys are leaking protein, which normally helps hold fluid inside your blood vessels. To determine the specific cause of this kidney condition, I am requesting a biopsy to look at the tissue directly.

REQUEST TEST: Kidney_Biopsy
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS
It is very unusual for a biopsy and a 24-hour collection to appear normal when your other tests show such high protein levels and fatty casts. Since these findings together strongly

I'm just as confused as you are, Doctor, especially since those earlier tests seemed to show something was wrong. Is it possible for the results to change that quickly, or could we have missed something? My legs still feel like they're filled with lead, and I'm still feeling very worn out.

It is possible that the standard tests aren't showing the full picture yet, but the "normal" biopsy results under a regular microscope actually point us toward a specific condition called Minimal Change Disease. To

Minimal Change Disease? I've never heard of that before, but if it explains why I'm so swollen and tired, I'm glad we have a name for it. Does this mean my kidneys aren't working right despite the biopsy looking normal at first?

Exactly; in Minimal Change Disease, the kidneys look normal under a regular microscope, but the filters are actually damaged at a microscopic level. Have you recently had any viral infections or immunizations before these symptoms started

No, I haven't had any shots or been sick with a cold or anything like that recently. These symptoms just seemed to come out of nowhere about ten days ago. I’ve just been dealing with my usual chronic bronchitis, but nothing new until this hit me.

Drafting response:
"Have you experienced any fevers, night sweats, or noticed any lumps or swollen glands in your neck, armpits, or groin? These details can help me determine
No, I haven't had any fevers or night sweats at all. I haven't noticed any lumps or swollen glands anywhere either. It’s really just been the swelling and this constant feeling of being worn out.

Since your biopsy appears normal under a standard microscope despite the heavy protein loss, I am confident this is Minimal Change Disease. I will now prepare a treatment plan, typically involving steroids, to help your

That sounds like a relief to finally have a plan, though the idea of taking steroids is new to me. Will that help get rid of the swelling in my legs and bring my energy back? I just want to feel like myself again and stop losing weight.

Yes, the steroids should help reduce the protein loss and resolve the swelling, though we will monitor your weight and nutrition closely. Since your biopsy appeared normal under standard light, this confirms the diagnosis of Minimal
That's good to hear, because I'm tired of my legs feeling so heavy all the time. How long does it usually take for the medicine to start working? I'm hoping I can get back to my normal routine soon.

Most patients start to see an improvement in their swelling within a few weeks of starting treatment. It was a pleasure to help you today, and I hope you feel much better soon.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Minimal Change Disease
